quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane use control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a traffic lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park" when parked on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so the car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may slip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until the intersection is clear before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers then proceed in the order they arrived at the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do as you approach the top of a hill?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. Adjust your speed so you can stop if a vehicle is stopped on the road ahead.

questions.question: When you reach a stop sign at an intersection with no painted crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: Stop inside the unmarked crosswalk.
Stop before entering the unmarked crosswalk.
Stop at the sign. It does not matter if you are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Stop completely before entering the crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn where it is posted.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down by taking your foot off the gas and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Not following them can result in a penalty.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space ahead and avoid braking suddenly. Slow down gradually or move to another lane to prevent a collision.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. If you are following this driver, be prepared for them to turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Change in direction ahead.
School zone and crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a two-way road.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for traffic, then go if it is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Fines for speeding are tripled in work and school zones.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Fines for speeding are doubled in work zones when workers are present and in school zones during school hours. Always drive carefully near workers and children.

questions.question: What should you do when making an emergency roadside stop?

options.text: Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Put your car in park and set the parking brake.
Leave your engine running and exit the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put your car in park and set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: During an emergency roadside stop, signal and pull as far off the road as possible. Then shift to park and set the parking brake. Turn on your emergency flashers and turn off the engine. Check for traffic before exiting.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: Three seconds.
Five seconds.
Seven seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of space between your car and the car ahead. Increase this distance in bad weather or poor road conditions.

questions.question: When should you enter a roundabout?

options.text: Only when there is a safe gap in traffic.
Anytime, because traffic entering always has the right-of-way.
After coming to a complete stop and checking both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when there is a safe gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: You must yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Enter only when you see a safe gap in traffic.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of a railroad crossing ahead. Be extra careful when approaching railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you leave the scene of a crash, your license can be suspended for how long?

options.text: Three months
Six months
Nine months
One year

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: If you are convicted of leaving the scene of a crash, your license can be suspended for up to one year.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians crossing on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to get across before a train comes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down to exit the interstate?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed shown on the exit ramp sign.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under bad conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed under good conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Slow down for school zones, work zones, bad weather, or construction. If conditions are unsafe, drive below the speed limit.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because a train is unlikely to come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park a car.
A place where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.
